To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an automated FLIM plate reader that can be used to quantify protein‐protein interactions and that we have demonstrated this capability using HIV Gag protein aggregation as a test case.
we have developed an automated FLIM plate reader that is able to measure protein aggregation in a high throughput manner.
we have demonstrated the first automated multiwell plate FLIM HCA reader and its application as a quantitative assay of protein aggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel optical techniques and instrumentation for high content analysis (hCA) of biological processes, with applications in drug screening and basic research.
the design of a new type of fluorescence lifetime imaging plate readers (FLIPR) for the high content analysis ( HCA ) of biomolecular interactions in live and fixed biological cells.
the development and application of fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) for high‐content analysis (HCA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have developed a new FLIM‐based plate reader that is suitable for the investigation of PPIs.
the FLIM‐FRET assay described here is a robust, quantitative and high content assay for the study of PPIs.
this paper is a nice example of how to use FLIM for FRET analysis in a high-throughput format.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an automated FLIM plate reader for HCA and applied it to the HIV‐1 Gag PPI.
we have developed a new technology for the analysis of protein interactions in cells.
we have developed an automated fluorescence lifetime imaging plate-reader and demonstrated its utility in the study of protein aggregation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FLIM HCA platform is a viable approach to assay protein aggregation and other PPIs, and that FLIM FRET can be used to generate quantitative dose response curves for inhibitor studies.
we have developed a high content fluorescence lifetime imaging plate-reader that can be used to measure Förster Resonant Energy Transfer (FRET) in biological samples.
FLIM HCA can be performed in a high throughput format, with the ability to perform rapid optically sectioned measurements of fixed and live cell samples.
